Date: 2026-09-21
Package source: C:/Users/yunti/OneDrive/Documentos/Clonotrace revision/Clonotrace-revised

Release summary

Version 1.2.0 consolidates the methodological and engineering revisions made during the benchmark work into the main Clonotrace package. The two principal changes are:

  1. the revised clone distance is now an audited, reusable package method and is the default result returned by clone_disance(); and
  2. the memory-conscious blocked/HDF5 bootstrap is now the default label_spreading_bootstrap() backend.

The unrevised Clonotrace distance and the legacy dense bootstrap remain available explicitly, so old results can still be reproduced and the revised distance can be evaluated against a raw-distance ablation.

Improvements accumulated to date

Version Area Main improvement
1.0.0 Initial method Clone-level modeling of lineage-resolved single-cell RNA data.
1.1.0 Scale and downstream analysis Blocked label spreading, HDF5 helpers, clone diffusion pseudotime, cell-clone coembedding, profile enrichment, and pseudotime-aware differential expression.
1.1.1 Correctness and reproducibility Validated distance conversion, robust checkpoints, exact/approximate separation, exact-OT safety limits, stable clone identifiers, explicit coembedding inputs, and clean-session tests/CI.
1.1.2 Cell-graph metric Corrected the SNN similarity-to-cost conversion used by shortest paths and versioned the cell-graph cache.
1.2.0 Clone-distance revision and bootstrap default Added local distance rescaling plus an optional clone-centroid component; made the revised distance and blocked bootstrap the defaults while retaining raw/legacy modes.

1. Correct cell-graph distance

The cell graph is constructed as an SNN graph, whose edge weights are shared neighbor similarities. Shortest-path routines interpret larger edge weights as longer costs, so the similarity must first be converted to a cost. The package now assigns the transformed graph returned by igraph::set_edge_attr() and uses

edge cost = exp(-shared-neighbor similarity)

Thus, stronger local transcriptomic similarity gives a shorter traversal cost. The graph-checkpoint metadata records this transform, preventing an older graph with untransformed similarities from being silently reused.

2. Safer exact and approximate clone distances

  • Exact OT and approximate nearest-neighbor distances have separate checkpoint files: clone_graph_dis_exact.rds and clone_graph_dis.rds.
  • Checkpoints carry input and parameter metadata and are written atomically. An incompatible cache now produces an actionable error rather than being silently reused.
  • Exact mode has conservative cell- and clone-count guards. A large run must be acknowledged explicitly with force_exact = TRUE.
  • Disconnected clone-bearing graph components and non-finite distances are detected explicitly.
  • long2square() now rejects missing, duplicate, or conflicting clone pairs.
  • Approximate graph-distance calculation supports clone blocking to limit peak memory.

These changes make exact OT usable as a reference calculation without treating it as the routine large-dataset default.

3. Revised clone distance

The new exported function revise_clone_distance() integrates the revised-distance branch into the main package. Starting with a raw Clonotrace clone-distance matrix, it performs three steps.

Local rescaling

For clone i, let sigma_i be its distance to the local_k-th nearest clone. The locally rescaled distance is

D_local(i,j) = D_raw(i,j) / sqrt(sigma_i * sigma_j)

This reduces distortions caused by unequal clone density in different parts of the clone manifold.

Clone-centroid distance

The method calculates Euclidean distance between clone centroids in the input RNA embedding. Exact observed clone labels are preferred; otherwise the cell-by-clone probability matrix supplies weights.

Fate-blind blend selection

After pairwise-median normalization, the final distance is

D_revised = (1 - s) * D_local + s * D_centroid

If s is not fixed by the user, Clonotrace selects it by maximizing Spearman agreement with clone RNA-cluster-composition differences over multiple Leiden resolutions, then uses the median selected weight. This selection does not use fate labels or benchmark outcomes, but it is RNA-cluster-informed. Therefore, benchmark reports should retain raw, local-rescaled, and full-revision ablations where relevant.

Additional integration details:

  • clone_disance() now returns the revised distance in dis by default.
  • The raw exact/approximate result is retained in dis_clonotrace.
  • revised = FALSE reproduces the pre-1.2 distance behavior.
  • Named and positional clone identifiers are supported.
  • A named clone-to-sample vector can restrict normalization and automatic weight selection to within-sample pairs.
  • A fixed mean_weight supports controlled ablations.
  • Selected weights, per-resolution choices, selection curves, raw distance, and local scales are retained as attributes for auditing.
  • Expensive raw OT/NN checkpoints are independent of the inexpensive revision parameters, so tuning the revision does not recompute the raw distance.

4. Blocked label-propagation bootstrap is now the default

label_spreading_bootstrap() now dispatches to the HDF5-backed blocked implementation unless backend = "dense" is requested explicitly. The blocked implementation:

  • fixes the global label-to-column mapping once, so bootstrap subsets cannot reorder clone classes;
  • processes clone classes in bounded blocks;
  • streams bootstrap/reference comparisons through HDF5;
  • preserves an HDF5 reference cache supplied by the caller;
  • removes only internally owned temporary files; and
  • guards deviance normalization when a cell has no eligible replicate.

This resolves the main avoidable source of bootstrap peak memory. It does not make the whole workflow disk-only: the final cells-by-clones probability matrix is still returned densely for compatibility. Worker count and block size must therefore still be selected conservatively.

5. Downstream and interface improvements

  • cell_clone_coembed() requires its cell-by-clone probability input explicitly, avoiding hidden dependence on a global variable.
  • Leiden helpers avoid ambiguous S4 dist dispatch and preserve clone names.
  • Clone-level diffusion pseudotime is available through clone_dpt().
  • Profile enrichment and pseudotime-aware profile differential-expression helpers are included.
  • Documentation now distinguishes clone-profile identity from cell-type annotation and records the new defaults and their compatibility switches.
  • Cross-platform R package checks and isolated-install validation are defined in GitHub Actions.

Compatibility notes

Intentional default changes

  1. clone_disance(..., revised = TRUE) is now the default. Use revised = FALSE for an unrevised exact-OT or approximate distance.
  2. label_spreading_bootstrap(..., backend = "blocked") is now the default. Use backend = "dense" only for legacy reproduction or small inputs.

The misspelled public function name clone_disance() is retained to avoid an API-breaking rename in this release.

Recommended benchmark reporting

For a method-comparison figure, report at least:

  • raw Clonotrace distance;
  • locally rescaled distance; and
  • full revised distance.

Automatic blend selection is fate-blind, but because it uses multiresolution RNA structure it should not be described as completely independent of RNA cluster organization.

The base-R regression suite covers the corrected SNN cost, long-to-square validation, cache validation and atomic writes, clone-identifier preservation, raw approximate and exact distance workflows, revised-distance construction, the internal automatic Leiden ladder used for centroid-weight selection, and the blocked-bootstrap default.

A full local vignette render was not possible because Pandoc is absent from the selected WSL environment. The GitHub Actions workflow installs Pandoc before building and checking the package, so the final repository check should render the vignette and remove the two local inst/doc warnings.

Deliberately not included in Clonotrace 1.2.0

  • Dataset-specific benchmark scoring, diagnostic figures, and competitor adapters remain analysis code and belong in a separate ClonoBench package if they are to be generalized.
  • Experimental disk-backed exact-OT/graph-flow prototypes remain outside this release until their API, numerical equivalence, and failure recovery are validated.
  • Simulation-specific fate fields and benchmark ground-truth construction are not part of the Clonotrace package.

This boundary keeps Clonotrace focused on the reusable biological method while allowing benchmark machinery to evolve independently.

Files most relevant to the release

  • R/clone_dis.R: corrected graph costs, validated checkpoints, exact/approx workflows, and revised-distance dispatch.
  • R/revised_distance.R: local rescaling, centroid distance, and automatic or fixed blend selection.
  • R/label_propagation.R: blocked-default bootstrap and legacy dense backend.
  • NEWS.md: concise user-facing version history.
  • vignettes/Clonotrace.Rmd: workflow examples and compatibility guidance.
  • tests/regression-base.R and tests/testthat/: release regression tests.
